title: Which population can the sample speak for
subtitle: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error  · 1 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **1 of the official questions in Inference from sample statistics and margin of error  are this one** — 0 Easy, 1 Medium, 0 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The sample was drawn from only one subgroup (one species, one class, one type), and the answer choices make claims about different scopes: the whole population, only that subgroup, the average, or a majority.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Identify exactly which group was randomly sampled.
- 2) Pick the choice that carries the sample statistic over to THAT group only, using the same statistic (a percent stays a percent) and hedged with 'approximately'.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Not applicable: this is purely a reasoning question and involves no computation.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You extend the result to a broader population that wasn't sampled, such as all fish instead of the one species sampled.
Or you turn a percent-above-a-threshold into a claim about the average or the majority.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You extend the result to a broader population that wasn't sampled, such as all fish instead of the one species sampled.
